scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8872: Users in BOTH pods report the entire data center is
gone: from host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1, every 10.200.0.x address times out,
DNS queries to 10.200.0.2 time out, and no portal loads by name or by IP.
Pod-to-pod traffic between the two user hosts still works. The server team
says the servers themselves are up and can still ping each other and their
gateway 10.200.0.1. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on switch_server_access and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_server_access ospfd
Mechanism: switch_server_access is the server farm's L3 edge: it owns the
  farm gateway 10.200.0.1 on br0 and advertises 10.200.0.0/24 into OSPF
  area 0 over its uplink to router_core_3 (172.16.0.10/31). With ospfd
  killed, zebra flushes its OSPF-learned routes immediately, so replies
  leaving the farm via 10.200.0.1 have no route back to 10.1.1.0/24 or
  10.2.1.0/24 and die at the gateway; the backbone then ages out its LSAs
  and withdraws 10.200.0.0/24. Farm-internal L2 and the gateway address
  itself keep working (bridging and zebra are untouched), and pod-to-pod
  traffic never crosses this device.
Localization: switch_server_access
Root cause: ospfd not running on switch_server_access
Fix: restart FRR on switch_server_access (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on switch_server_access" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on switch_server_access (`service frr restart`).
The OSPF config lives in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process,
not the file), so a plain restart reloads it, 10.200.0.0/24 is re-advertised
into area 0, and both pods regain the server farm.
scoring_axes: bonus-rules-out-l2: notes farm-internal reachability and the 10.200.0.1 gateway still work, so the fault is L3/OSPF on switch_server_access, not the bridge or the servers

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The OSPF routing daemon (`ospfd`) on `switch_server_access` — the FRR device that connects the server subnet (10.200.0.0/24) to the rest of the network via `router_core_3:eth2 ↔ switch_server_access:eth5`.

**Mechanism:** `switch_server_access` has no OSPF process running (`ospfd=no`) and carries zero `network` statements in FRR. Because OSPF never starts on this device, it never forms an adjacency with `router_core_3` on their shared /31 point-to-point link (172.16.0.10/31 in area 0.0.0.0). As a direct consequence: (1) the server prefix 10.200.0.0/24 is never originated into OSPF, so every other router in the domain — including the distribution-layer gateways `switch_dist_1_1` (10.1.1.1) and `switch_dist_2_1` (10.2.1.1) — has no route for it, and (2) `switch_server_access` itself holds no learned routes and therefore cannot forward any return traffic toward the user subnets.

**Localization:** Fault is entirely on `switch_server_access`. `router_core_3` is healthy: it has OSPF active in area 0.0.0.0 on eth2 and is ready to form an adjacency, but its peer never responds. All other routers have full OSPF adjacencies and correct route tables within the domain they can reach.

**Root cause:** OSPF is completely absent on `switch_server_access` — no daemon, no network statements — severing the server subnet from the routing domain.

**Fix:** Enable `ospfd` on `switch_server_access` and add `network 10.200.0.0/24 area 0.0.0.0` (plus the uplink 172.16.0.11/31 in area 0.0.0.0) to its FRR configuration. This will bring up the OSPF adjacency with `router_core_3`, inject 10.200.0.0/24 into the OSPF domain, and restore bidirectional reachability between users and all data-centre services.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the fault to switch_server_access (ospfd absent on that device).
The agent explicitly states ospfd is not running on switch_server_access (no daemon/no network statements), correctly identifying the OSPF daemon as down.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-l2: notes farm-internal reachability and the 10.200.0.1 gateway still work, so the fault is L3/OSPF on switch_server_access, not the bridge or the servers
per_axis.rationale: The report identifies an OSPF absence on switch_server_access but does not state that farm-internal L2/bridging and the 10.200.0.1 gateway remain functional, which the axis requires.
Enabling/starting ospfd and ensuring the server and uplink networks are present will restore the OSPF adjacency and re-advertise 10.200.0.0/24, accomplishing the same fix as restarting FRR.

The agent's observations (ping failures with 'Destination Net Unreachable' and the ospf_snapshot showing ospfd=no, no network statements, and 0 neighbors on the server-access device) directly support its diagnosis that OSPF is absent on switch_server_access and that this severs the server subnet from the domain. The investigation and writeup logically connect the evidence to the root cause and proposed fix.
